data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Reading comprehension involves understanding an existing text; panel judgment involves applying a rule to new data.","The perturbation in reading tests is textual; in panels, it is the decision rule itself.","Understanding a text and understanding a checklist's causal role in an outcome are different cognitive tasks."],"overturn_conditions":["If the panel maintains high performance under rephrasing, this supports the understanding residual and the reliability gain.","If the panel fails under rephrasing but the expert also fails under analogous perturbation, the distinction is moot.","If the rephrased checklist is objectively harder to apply (e.g., more ambiguous), a performance drop does not prove mere compliance."],"shared_structure":["Both involve a distinction between syntactic matching (compliance) and semantic abstraction (understanding).","Both predict that a true grasp of the underlying structure should be invariant to surface form.","Both imply that performance dependent on surface form is a sign of a fragile, non-generalizable mechanism."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_005"],"transfer_claims":["If panelists genuinely understand the checklist, their accuracy should be invariant to rephrasing, just as reading comprehension is invariant to paraphrase.","A collapse in performance under rephrasing indicates the panel was relying on surface features (compliance) rather than deep features (understanding), just as poor performance on paraphrased texts indicates shallow reading.","The presence of an understanding residual in the panelist's cognitive model is what distinguishes a robust reliability gain from a brittle compliance artifact."]},"claim":"The distinguishing mark of mere checklist compliance is that panel performance will catastrophically collapse when the checklist is reordered or rephrased, while a genuine reliability gain reflects a deep understanding residual that is invariant to the form of the checklist. A panel following an explicit checklist will, on average, produce more reliable judgments because the checklist acts as an externalized cognitive scaffold, but this is true only if panelists possess an understanding residual that survives formal reordering.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the rephrased checklist is functionally equivalent but panel performance collapses, the original gain was mere compliance, and the covering principle is false for that panel.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If no understanding residual exists (performance is entirely explained by the checklist score), the panel cannot adapt to any distributional shift.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the reordering is so extreme that it breaks the semantic coherence of the checklist, even understanding panelists will fail, making this a false negative.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert's intuition is actually a form of implicit checklist-following, the distinction between compliance and understanding is illusory.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Mere compliance tracks the right answer by superficial lexical or sequential matching to a trained template. Genuine reliability gain stems from a causal understanding of the checklist's items that allows panelists to reweight or reorder features mentally. If panelists rely solely on compliance, their performance is brittle; if they possess an understanding residual, their performance is robust to perturbation.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
